title: Sunday Beach Clean-up
intro: Text 1 is a social media post by a volunteer group that cleans up beaches.

visual.text: The sea keeps returning what we throw away. This Sunday, help us take it back.
Changi Beach clean-up · Sunday, 7.30 am · all hands welcome
A girl of about fourteen holds up a single faded slipper tangled in fishing line. Behind her, volunteers with tongs and sacks spread out across the sand at sunrise.

Last month we found bottles, straws, slippers and even a rice cooker — all before breakfast. None of it belongs on a beach where children dig and crabs make their homes. You do not need to be fit or know anything about the sea. If you can bend down and pick something up, you are qualified.

visual.title: What to expect
items: We bring: gloves, tongs, sacks and a weighing scale
You bring: a water bottle, a hat and covered shoes
Afterwards: teh and curry puffs on us

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a blog post by Shalini, a student who joined her first beach clean-up.
paragraphs: I almost did not go. I am not sporty, and I could not tell you the name of a single fish, but nobody there seemed to mind. A woman in a wide straw hat handed me a pair of tongs and pointed at a stretch of sand that looked perfectly clean. It was not.

Once I started looking, I saw bottle caps, sweet wrappers and crumbs of foam everywhere, mixed in with the shells. By nine o’clock my sack was so heavy that I had to drag it. My strangest find was a plastic toy soldier, its paint long gone. Some child had lost it years ago, and the sea had carried it all the way to Changi. I keep thinking about how long it must have been floating.

Look at the picture in Text 1. What does it show, and how does that support the headline ‘The sea keeps returning what we throw away. This Sunday, help us take it back.’?

scheme.answer: It shows a girl holding up an old slipper caught in fishing line while volunteers clear the beach behind her; the slipper is rubbish the sea has brought back, and the volunteers are taking it back, as the headline asks.
points: It shows a girl holding up a faded slipper tangled in fishing line, with volunteers collecting rubbish on the beach behind her. [1]
This backs the headline: the slipper is rubbish the sea has washed back, and the volunteers are ‘taking it back’ by clearing the sand. [1]

seeds.text: The picture shows a girl holding up an old slipper stuck in fishing line, and people with sacks and tongs behind her. This supports the headline because the slipper is the rubbish the sea brought back to the beach, and the volunteers are taking it away like the headline asks.

We see a girl showing a worn-out slipper wrapped in fishing line while other volunteers pick up rubbish on the sand. The slipper proves the sea washes our rubbish back, and the people cleaning show readers how to help take it back.

It supports the headline because it proves that the sea really does wash our rubbish back onto the beach, so we must help to remove it.
